content.text:
I submitted **#106** (Fe 0.60, Ni 0.26, V 0.14) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, 2.4e-7 A.

All three merit measurements are used:

| Index | Fe / Ni / V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 99 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 | 0 |
| 83 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 | 1.5e-7 |
| 106 | 0.60 / 0.26 / 0.14 | 2.4e-7 |

Photocurrent went up as the vanadium fraction went down and iron went up. The composition with equal Fe and V gave nothing. I spent the last measurement on the Fe-rich, V-poor corner.

What this doesn't cover:
- **Unmeasured regions:** I never measured anything in the V-rich (above 0.6 V) or Ni-rich (above 0.6 Ni) parts of the library. A better composition could be there.
- **Unused suggestion:** The Gaussian-process model's top suggestion was #145 (Fe 0.54, Ni 0.24, V 0.22). I didn't measure it and chose #106 because it has less V.
- **No XRD:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so I don't know which crystal phases these films contain.
